question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the cosecant-cotangent identity 

$$
1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic cosecant-cotangent identity

$$
{coth}^{2}⁡\theta -1={csch}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Setting $\theta =7x-2,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{coth}^{2}⁡(7x-2)-1 & ={csch}^{2}⁡(7x-2) \\ {coth}^{2}⁡(7x-2) & ={csch}^{2}⁡(7x-2)+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{csch}^{3}⁡(7x-2)+\operatorname{csch}⁡(7x-2)}{\operatorname{coth}⁡(7x-2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡(7x-2)[{csch}^{2}⁡(7x-2)+1]}{\operatorname{coth}⁡(7x-2)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡(7x-2){coth}^{2}⁡(7x-2)}{\operatorname{coth}⁡(7x-2)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{csch}⁡(7x-2)\operatorname{coth}⁡(7x-2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{7}\operatorname{csch}⁡(7x-2)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
